summary: Forestry lookout on Shoulder Mountain near Topley Landing, Babine Lake; only a 1977 staffing notice and an undated travel-directory mention found.

facts.status_note: Only an undated travel directory describes a lookout there; no source confirms its condition.

visit.trail_note: An undated travel directory lists a trail leading up to the lookout.

events.note: Planned staffing per a June 1, 1977 Lake District News item (quoted by Canada Lookouts): primary site to be manned, secondary site on Deesius Mountain to stay vacant unless patrolled.

evidence.supports: 1977 staffing notice for the primary and secondary sites
evidence.quote: The primary lookout site on Shoulder Mountain will be manned but the secondary site on Deesius Mountain east of Babine Lake will be vacant unless manned on a patrol basis during extreme conditions.

evidence.supports: trail to a forestry lookout on Shoulder Mountain near Topley Landing
evidence.quote: there is a trail leading up to a forestry lookout on Shoulder Mountain near Topley Landing

evidence.supports: Shoulder Mountain named among areas popular for snowmobiling in winter (the paragraph is about the winter season)
evidence.quote: Burns Lake, Shoulder Mountain and the backcountry roads near Granisle and Smithers Landing in the Babine Lake region are popular for snowmobiling

notes_for_editor: Built date, builder, fate and access level are not in any source found, so those keys are omitted. The listing's elevation (Elev. 1220) has no unit and is left out of the story; the brief reads it as metres. The travel-directory line is undated and is the only evidence the tower still stands. The 1977 quote is secondhand via Canada Lookouts; the Lake District News original was not read. Two WebSearch calls used. The BC Archives fire-lookout listing could not be read (certificate errors in both fetch_text and WebFetch).
